Hard constraints: no phone numbers, message or review text in logs; review data retention
observations: O-66-1 (unconfirmed, no change): deliver() writes provider_message_id in a separate statement after the provider returns; a 'delivered' status callback arriving before that write matches no row and is dropped (Twilio does not retry status callbacks). Only lowers the report's delivered count; in practice the write takes milliseconds and 'delivered' comes seconds later.
O-66-2 (no change): review_requests.provider_message_id has no index, so each delivery receipt scans review_requests. Fine at pilot size; add an index if the table grows.

O-66-3 (no change): every Twilio use (review requests, the inbound STOP webhook, confirmations) now reads TWILIO_STATUS_CALLBACK_URL, so a malformed value makes the inbound webhook answer 503 'not configured'. Misconfiguration only; unset is fine.

O-66-4 (SPEC question, not a bug): Twilio may later report a text it accepted as 'undelivered' or 'failed'. FR-6 says email only when the text fails; main treats an accepted text as sent and never falls back to email on a later carrier failure. #66 reads those statuses but ignores them. Owner to decide whether a carrier failure counts as 'the text fails'.
O-62-1 (no change): job-run audit rows (about 480 a day) are never purged; IDs and job names only, so no personal data, but audit_log grows without bound.

#63: failure details hold a sanitized code only (Resend name regex, Twilio numeric code, class name); one alert per location, kind and period via a prefix match on detail; offboarded businesses excluded.
#62: the route returns job names, states and times only; a run that throws inside a step is recorded as failed, so a working scheduler never reads as late.
unresolved: O-66-1..O-66-4, O-62-1 (observations; O-66-4 needs an owner decision)
